Subject: Post-demo: Fintegro integration orchestration checklist & routing policy

Alex / Priya — thanks again for taking the demo today. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our side so engineering can start planning integration: 

Summary of needs (what we heard)
- Real-time customer support assistant embedded in product UI (low single-digit latency target for short completions).
- Sensitive PII in prompts; must route through Private deployment in us-east for certain tenants (HIPAA-like constraints).
- Multi-model strategy: concise answers from a cheaper 8-bit quantized model for standard flows, optional higher-quality model for escalations and code generation.
- Re-ranker on search results (embedding-based) for KB retrieval.
- SSO + SCIM for user provisioning, and token-based service auth for backend SDK calls.

Proposed integration checklist (actionable items)
1) SDK & auth
   - We will provide the Node + Python SDK quickstart bundle (attached: sdk_auth_quickstart.zip).
   - Preferred setup: server-side service token for inference, rotated via KMS. For admin tooling and auditing use our OAuth flow + SCIM for provisioning.
   - Ask: can Fintegro support service account keys stored in their secrets manager (Y/N)? If yes, send preferred KMS provider.

2) Routing & policy configuration (draft)
   - Region routing: traffic from EU users -> eu model pool, US users -> us-east by default. For tenant-scoped private data, force route to Private us-east cluster.
   - Latency/cost policy tiers:
       * Realtime UI (SLO: p95 <= 300ms for <256 tokens): route to low-latency CPU/GPU pool with batching disabled; cost-aware fallback to cheaper quantized variant after 150ms.
       * Background summarization (no strict SLO): batch for cost savings and use 4-bit quantized models.
   - Fallback chain example for UI requests:
       1. primary: rwd-gtp-7b-fp16 (low-latency GPU)
       2. fallback1: rwd-7b-q4 (quantized, cheaper)
       3. fallback2: rwd-ggml-2b (on-prem/private CPU)
   - Re-ranker: embeddings stored in your S3; Redwood will run embedding generation during ingestion and provide a reranker endpoint.

3) Structured output & tool calling
   - We'll expose function/tool calling via the SDK so the assistant can call your internal ticketing API. Define the pointer schema and we'll wire the function signature.

4) Security & compliance
   - For tenants requiring private processing we recommend Private deployment with customer-managed VPC and KMS. Audit logs will be forwarded to your SIEM (we support syslog/S3 sinks).

Next steps / timeline
- By EOD Wed 08/05: Fintegro to confirm service account KMS provider and whether any tenant needs Private routing initially (Priya?).
- By Fri 08/07: Redwood to share routing_policy_proposal.md (attached) with recommended JSON policy templates and sample fallback chains.
- Schedule a 60m technical review with your infra + security — suggested windows next Tue/Wed. Grace / Stephanie can own that from our side.

Attachments: fintegro_msp_requirements.pdf (PDF), routing_policy_proposal.md (markdown), sdk_auth_quickstart.zip (zip)
